correctness.rationale: Three agents and four strictly positive additive goods imply every EF1 terminal bundle cardinality is (2,1,1); the singleton holder i must value her own good at least the smaller (in her values) of the doubled holder’s two goods. Because only order matters, exact four-value multisets reduce to four agent-specific ranks used once each; tied values can be tie-broken conservatively. The finite perfect-information game has adversary arrival triple first and recipient response second, so the forall-arrival/exists-recipient Bellman recursion proves policy existence or adversarial obstruction. An independently reimplemented memoized rank recursion returned unrestricted=True (115651 states), first_two_distinct=True (104443), first_two_together=False (24681), first_three_distinct=False (21189), precisely matching source Python counts. Inspected paired C++ numeric checker and negative witness tree path conventions, though not independently replayed 52-kB tree file. The finite game exhausts all possible predicted order assignments and is not merely a horizon sample.

evidence: Published 3-agent 3-level/no-prediction positive theorem covers a smaller valuation alphabet, whereas here predicted arbitrary four distinct levels (with repeats allowed). Other results treat 2 agents, 3 goods or weaker 1/2-EF1.
